solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Paint or paper I ordered is not suitable

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, matching the answer

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of the preceding words are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone choosing decorations decides that the paint or wallpaper isn't right for the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' sounds like buying the paint and paper, but it signals that the thirteen letters of PAINT OR PAPER I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something unfitting or out of place for an occasion is improper.

clue.text: They are not suited for camp life

definitions.text: They are not suited for camp life

parts.words: They are not suited for camp life
parts.note: not suited plays on wearing no suit (no clothes at all), and camp is a naturist camp

explanation.surface: Some people are just not cut out for roughing it under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists at a holiday camp go without clothes, so they are literally un-suited.

clue.text: Duet involving piano melody

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A duet that includes a piano and a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a duet is performed by two people, a couple of performers.

clue.text: Tackle some vote-manipulating

definitions.meaning: a ship's ropes and gear, its tackle
fixing an election, as in ballot fraud

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a sailing ship's ropes and gear, and the act of fixing a ballot dishonestly.

clue.text: Adage showing preference for a word of action

parts.note: being pro something means favouring it, a preference for it
a verb is the part of speech naming an action

explanation.surface: A saying that reveals a liking for doing things rather than talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an adage is a traditional saying, a short piece of folk wisdom.

clue.text: 'Children causing trouble are somewhat dim' — psychologist

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A psychologist sums up naughty children as being a bit slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'are', but that word is only the link joining definition to wordplay; the definition is the plural noun phrase 'Children causing trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mischievous children are often called little devils or rascals.

clue.text: Conrad's whirlwind romance?

parts.note: Joseph Conrad wrote a novella with this title, and the word is also a tropical storm

explanation.surface: A novelist's sudden love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a violent tropical whirlwind and the title of a Joseph Conrad story.

clue.text: Marathon perhaps?

parts.note: a marathon run can be a long struggle, and Marathon was also a famous battle

explanation.surface: Is this a long-distance race?
explanation.walkthrough: Marathon is both a long footrace and an ancient Greek battle, so it is literally a battle connected with running.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn-out conflict; Marathon, a battle that gave its name to a race, fits literally.

clue.text: Plot associated with vice?

parts.note: a vice is a gripping tool, so a plot linked to one would grip; also a thrilling tale

explanation.surface: A scheme connected with wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping tale is an enthralling narrative; a vice is a clamp that grips.

clue.text: Returning antelope occupied by kill gets coup de grace

indicators.note: occupied by means the other piece goes inside this one
returning means the word for the antelope is read backwards

parts.note: a gnu is an African antelope, the wildebeest
to do in is slang for to kill

explanation.surface: A hunter's finishing blow comes when a fleeing antelope is cornered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses the antelope to UNG, and 'occupied by' places the slang for kill within it; 'coup de grace' looks French but is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The coup de grace is the final blow that brings about someone's ruin or downfall.

clue.text: It's to do with examination in theory

definitions.meaning: an exam taken in written form, as opposed to oral or practical
something true in principle but perhaps not in practice

explanation.definitionFit: A written exam is sat in writing; a plan that only works in theory looks good in writing.

clue.text: It detects by smell and is aware by sound

indicators.note: by sound means the word for being aware is said aloud

parts.note: to know something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: Some sense organ that picks up smells and is alert to noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs two senses, but 'by sound' signals a homophone: KNOWS, said aloud, gives the spelling of the smelling organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The facial organ used for smelling detects odours.

clue.text: Cried out for a drink

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouted out an order at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cried out' looks like a single phrase meaning shouted, but 'out' rearranges the five letters of CRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fermented drink made from apples.

clue.text: Ring for house work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work of music

explanation.surface: Calling someone about chores at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a circular band, like a hula band or a barrel band, is a ring.

clue.text: Reports come back up when such charges are dropped

definitions.text: Reports come back up when such charges are dropped

parts.words: Reports come back up when such charges are dropped
parts.note: ... charges are dropped into the sea, and their explosions (reports) echo back to the surface

explanation.surface: Accusations are withdrawn and news resurfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges are dropped' reads like a court case ending, but these are underwater explosives whose bangs come back up.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-submarine explosives set to go off at a set distance below the surface.

clue.text: Gun is dismantled for practice

indicators.note: dismantled means the letters of the preceding words are taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A firearm is taken apart for training.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: putting something to use is the practice or employment of it.

clue.text: Is it to encourage laying in a little money?

definitions.text: Is it to encourage laying in a little money?

parts.words: Is it to encourage laying in a little money?
parts.note: a dummy egg left in a nest encourages a hen to lay, and laying in money means saving it

explanation.surface: A query about whether a gesture is meant to spur saving.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings set aside for the future, named after the fake egg put in a hen's nest.

clue.text: It normally lacks bark

parts.note: the African hunting dog that famously yodels rather than barks

explanation.surface: Some tree that usually has no outer covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' suggests a tree's covering; it is the dog's noise, and the Congo dog breed is known as barkless.
explanation.definitionFit: A small African dog breed known for being unable to bark in the usual way.

clue.text: Sideways?

parts.note: read as side ways, minor or secondary routes

explanation.surface: A question about moving laterally.
explanation.definitionFit: Side roads or minor tracks away from the main way.

clue.text: Old educational establishment to work with new figure

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of British college now largely renamed as universities
to go is to function or work, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: A former college joining forces with a fresh face.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a many-sided plane shape is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Exercise period in prison

definitions.meaning: to extend the limbs as a warm-up, a form of exercise
slang for a term served in jail

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an extending of the limbs, and slang for a jail term.

clue.text: Meaning to follow, being sheepish

parts.note: to get the hang of something is to get its meaning or drift
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: Someone trailing behind with an embarrassed look.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shamefaced, guilty look is a sheepish one.

clue.text: Intercept principal on holiday

parts.note: a head teacher is the principal of a school
someone off work is on holiday

explanation.surface: Catching the school head while away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to block or cut off someone's path is to intercept them.

clue.text: They depend on cattle and some old folk

definitions.text: They depend on cattle and some old folk

parts.words: They depend on cattle and some old folk
parts.note: depend is used literally, to hang down, as folds of loose skin hang from a neck

explanation.surface: Some people rely on livestock, as do certain elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depend on' reads as rely on, but means hang down from: loose folds of skin under the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Folds of loose skin hanging from the throat of cattle or older people.

clue.text: Be inclined to make a charge

definitions.meaning: to joust, charging with a lance

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to lean at an angle, and to charge at an opponent in a joust.

clue.text: Rest that a billiards player wants as high as possible?

definitions.text: Rest that a billiards player wants as high as possible?

parts.words: Rest that a billiards player wants as high as possible?
parts.note: a rest is a pause, and in billiards or snooker a run of scoring shots is scored, the higher the better

explanation.surface: A cue-sport player would like their cue support raised as far as it will go.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards a rest is a cue support, but here rest means a pause, and the word for a pause also names a player's scoring run.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause in work, and also a continuous scoring run in billiards or snooker.

clue.text: First sign of true intelligence in a fool

indicators.note: First sign of means take the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: wit is mental sharpness, intelligence

explanation.surface: Even a fool might show a glimmer of real brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a silly or foolish person, informally.

clue.text: Tendency to be dishonest

definitions.meaning: slang for corrupt, as a crooked police officer

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a natural leaning or talent, and slang for crooked or corrupt.

clue.text: Being near, aim

definitions.meaning: near is old-fashioned for stingy with money

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: tight-fisted (near), and to intend or have as purpose.

clue.text: Support for a runner in St Leger?

indicators.note: a runner in suggests the letters of the race name are running loose, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Backing a horse in a famous race at Doncaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger is an English flat horse race at Doncaster; 'a runner in' looks like a horse in the race but signals rearranging the letters of ST LEGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded stand on which a person raises and rests a tired limb is a kind of support.

clue.text: New opera in natural setting

indicators.note: New signals that the letters of the following words are made afresh in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh opera production staged among natural scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective on the opera, but it signals rearranging OPERA IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoors, under the sky, a setting in nature rather than a building.

clue.text: Not out of the running, after all

definitions.meaning: still in contention when a race ends

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: still involved when the race ends, and ultimately or in the end.
